title: NDSEARCH: Accelerating Graph-Traversal-Based Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search through Near Data Processing
problem: Graph-traversal-based ANNS algorithms achieve high recall but graph data exceeds main memory capacity as datasets grow. Limited SSD I/O bandwidth severely degrades performance when using SSD as backing storage.
motivation: ANNS is fundamental to vector databases and data center applications including person re-identification, recommendation systems, and retrieval augmented generation for large language models.
method: NDSeARCH is a hardware-software co-designed near-data processing solution featuring SEARSSD, an in-storage computing architecture that leverages LUN-level parallelism inside NAND flash chips to execute ANNS kernels. It employs two-level scheduling to improve data locality and exploit internal bandwidth, combined with speculative searching to accelerate ANNS workloads.
key_novelty: In-storage computing architecture (SEARSSD) that exploits LUN-level parallelism in NAND flash chips to perform ANNS computation near the data, eliminating SSD I/O bandwidth bottlenecks.
contributions: SEARSSD in-storage computing architecture supporting ANNS kernels with LUN-level parallelism
Two-level scheduling strategy to improve data locality and exploit internal bandwidth in near-data processing
Speculative searching mechanism for ANNS acceleration
Comprehensive hardware-software co-design achieving significant throughput and energy efficiency improvements

metrics.speedup: 31.7x over CPU, 14.6x over GPU, 7.4x over SmartSSD-only, 2.9x over DeepStore
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: Two orders-of-magnitude higher energy efficiency than CPU and GPU

primary_theme: In-storage computing for accelerating approximate nearest neighbor search
